parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> BeanWave Coffee (BWC) is a small roaster in country L. It buys green coffee beans from Brazil and pays in US dollars (USD). BWC sells roasted coffee to local cafés. The owner is considering buying a new semi-automatic roasting machine to improve quality and reduce roasting time. The machine costs L\$150 000. Staff would need training. Packaging is currently non-recyclable, and energy costs are rising.
> 
> **Table 1.1 – Exchange rate change and recent invoice**
> 
> | Item | Value |
> |---|---|
> | Last month’s bean invoice | **USD 12 000** |
> | Exchange rate before | **1 USD = L\$4.5** |
> | Exchange rate now | **1 USD = L\$5.0** |

Calculate the increase in L\$ cost of the USD 12 000 invoice caused by the exchange rate change shown in Table 1.1. Show your working.
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **L\$6 000**

**Calculation steps**

Calculate the cost before the rate change

`equals space 12 comma 000 space cross times space 4.5 space

equals space straight L $ 54 comma 000`

Calculate the cost now

`equals space 12 comma 000 space cross times space 5.0 space

equals space straight L $ 60 comma 000`**       [1]**

Calculate the cost increase

`equals space 60 comma 000 space minus space 54 comma 000 space

equals space straight L $ 6 comma 000`**          [1]**

> - Correct method but wrong final figure [1]

**Extract:**

**Sports Safety Equipment (SSE)**

SSE manufactures sports safety equipment in country Z. It is a public limited company which has been successful for over 30 years. The main product SSE manufactures is safety helmets for different sports, such as bicycle riding, cricket and skateboarding. SSE has one large factory making the safety helmets. The factory uses flow production. The production workers each specialise in one task on the production line. SSE’s raw materials are imported.

SSE sells its helmets in several other countries and is planning to expand into many more. It will need to carry out market research before entering new markets in other countries. Each country has different sports that are popular and the style of helmets varies from country to country.

SSE plans to build its own factories in its most important markets in other countries and will need to choose a suitable source of finance. The Human Resources Director has decided to use internal recruitment for the managers of the new factories. There will need to be effective communication between the managers of the new factories and SSE’s head office in country Z.

Most of SSE’s sales in country Z are through sports equipment shops. Customers like to try on the helmets to check they fit correctly. SSE currently sells its helmets in other countries through its website.

SSE is also increasing its product range. The latest new product being developed is a children’s cricket helmet. A break-even chart for this new product is shown in Appendix 3.

**Appendix 1 **

**Extract from SSE’s website **

**If you want the best protection when playing sport then buy an SSE safety helmet!**

We supply a wide range of safety helmets for you when playing sport.

Whatever the sport - SSE produces a helmet for you.

You can order directly from this website by entering your head measurements below.

Get the perfect fit for you!

**Appendix 2 **

**Email from SSE’s Managing Director to SSE’s Finance Director**

To: Finance Director

From: Managing Director

Date: 1 September 2023

Re: Demand for SSE’s products Demand for SSE’s products in country Z is forecast to increase. Our government has imposed import tariffs on safety helmets. We may be able to increase our prices.

The exchange rate in country Z is expected to fall. However, other countries have introduced import quotas on safety helmets.

We will have to consider all the likely effects of these changes.

**Appendix 3 **

**Projected weekly break-even chart for SSE’s new children’s cricket helmet**

The maximum output and sales for this product is 1000 units per week.

Consider how each of the following **three **changes may affect SSE.

- A depreciation in the currency of country Z
- An import tariff introduced on sports helmets imported into country Z
- Quotas introduced on sports helmets in countries where SSE sells its products

Which change is likely to have the greatest effect on SSE’s profit? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2023-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
A depreciation in country Z's currency would make SSE's exports of children's cricket helmets **[Ap] **cheaper and more competitive in other countries. This could increase sales and revenue from exports **[An]**. However, SSE's imported raw materials **[Ap] **would become more expensive, increasing costs **[An]**

An import tariff on sports helmets into country Z would make imported helmets more expensive compared to SSE's domestically-produced helmets **[Ap] **. This could allow SSE to increase its prices and market share in country Z, potentially boosting profits on sales there **[An]**

Quotas on sports helmet imports in SSE's export markets would limit the quantity of helmets SSE could sell in those countries. This may reduce SSE's sales and revenue from exports **[An]**. SSE plans to build its own factories in its most important markets in other countries **[Ap]**, which could be a way to bypass these quotas.

The depreciation of country Z's currency is likely to have the greatest effect on SSE's profit **[E] **. As SSE sells helmets in several other countries and plans to expand into many more **[Ap]**, the increased competitiveness of its exports could substantially boost sales volumes and revenue. While import costs would rise, the potential for significantly higher export sales could outweigh this, leading to the largest impact on overall profitability compared to the other changes **[E] **

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Depreciation of Country Z’s currency**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Exports of children’s cricket helmets become cheaper abroad → boosts competitiveness → increases sales and revenue
>     - Imported helmets cost more in Country Z → SSE’s own helmets gain price advantage at home → home-market sales rise
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Imports of raw materials for bicycle safety helmets become costlier → production costs increase → SSE may need to raise prices → sales may fall
> - **Import tariff on sports helmets into Country Z**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Tariff on imported competitor helmets raises their price → SSE’s helmets become more competitive → demand and revenue increase
>     - Competitors’ higher prices may allow SSE to raise its own prices without losing customers → revenue and profit rise
> - **Quotas on sports helmets in export markets**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Limited supply can drive up helmet prices abroad → SSE may maintain or increase revenue if demand holds
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Quotas cap the quantity SSE can export → restricts sales potential and caps revenue growth
>     - SSE must invest in local production facilities to bypass quotas → requires significant capital outlay
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Currency depreciation offers the greatest positive impact by expanding export volumes and home-market competitiveness, driving strong revenue gains
>   - Import tariffs provide a moderate boost to competitiveness and profits but depend on competitor presence and price sensitivity
>   - Quotas pose the most severe threat to export sales and force expensive local investment if limits are tight

**Extract:**

**Protective Hats (PH) **

PH is a large public limited company based in country Z. It has been operating successfully for 50 years. PH produces a range of protective hats for employees working on construction sites, in factories or mines. It has a reputation for producing high-quality products and sells its hats around the world.

PH is currently the market leader in country Z. To remain competitive PH regularly carries out market research to find out if new products are needed. PH needs to ensure its market research data is accurate, so that it can develop the best new protective hats.

PH’s only factory is in country Z. It has 100 production employees. They work on a flow production line and carry out the same tasks every day. PH pays these employees the minimum wage and there have been complaints about working conditions. Some of the employees are considering becoming members of a trade union.

PH’s directors plan to expand the company by opening factories in other countries to produce protective hats. They think there are many benefits for PH of becoming a multinational company. They are aware that there is growing demand for protective hats in many developing countries where construction and manufacturing industries are expected to continue to have strong growth in the next 10 years.

**Appendix 1 **

**Advertisement for PH’s products**

PH’s protective hats will protect your employees when at work. We supply many of the leading construction, manufacturing and mining companies across the world.

High quality is guaranteed.

PH’s hats can be ordered online from our website.

**Appendix 2 **

**Email to PH’s Managing Director from PH’s Human Resources Director**

To: Managing Director

From: Human Resources Director

Date: 1 October 2023

Re: Training

After reviewing our current training, I think we need to increase the training we provide to new employees. Existing employees would also benefit from additional training as there have been issues with motivation.

I know there are plans to introduce new equipment into the flow production line. When is this likely to happen?

Can we please meet to discuss these issues?

**Appendix 3 **

**PH’s financial data for 2021 and 2022**

|   | **2021** | **2022** |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | \$100m | \$125m |
| Profit | \$20m | \$20m |
| Gross profit margin | 60% | 65% |
| Profit margin | 20% | 16% |

Consider **three **possible benefits for PH of becoming a multinational company. Which benefit is likely to be the most important? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2023-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
PH could produce protective hats in countries with lower costs. This would reduce their production expenses, potentially allowing them to lower prices and become more competitive **[An]**. As PH currently only has one factory in country Z **[Ap]**, opening factories abroad could significantly cut costs **[An]**

Secondly, PH could gain easier access to raw materials in other countries. This could reduce transport costs and delivery times for materials needed to make protective hats **[Ap]**. Quicker access to materials could help PH respond faster to changing customer needs **[An]**

Thirdly, becoming multinational would help PH increase its market share. There is  growing demand for protective hats in developing countries where construction and manufacturing are expected to grow strongly **[Ap]**. By setting up factories in these countries, PH could more easily expand into these new markets and increase its sales **[An]**

The most important benefit is likely to be producing in countries with lower costs **[E]**. PH's profit margin fell from 20% to 16% between 2021 and 2022 **[Ap]**, suggesting they need to reduce costs. Lower production costs would allow PH to offer more competitive prices, which is crucial **[E] **as they face growing competition **[Ap]**. It would also help them maintain or increase their profit margin **[E]**. While accessing new markets is important, reducing costs would help PH compete more effectively in all markets, both existing and new **[E]**

Retailers have reported increased sales for most types of products such as sales of washing machines which have increased by 15%. Economic growth in country Y is predicted to increase.

Many businesses have been recruiting additional employees and there are now shortages of some skilled workers. The government in country Y has recorded an increase in inflation to 8% so far this year, which is a worry.

Consider the following **three **problems for SSM when entering markets in other countries.

- Cultural differences
- Lack of knowledge
- Import restrictions

Which problem is likely to have the most effect on SSM? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2021-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Cultural differences could pose issues for SSM, as soap powder preferences may vary between countries. SSM currently only sells to large retailers in country Y **[Ap]**. In new markets, consumers may prefer different scents **[Ap]**, packaging or product features that SSM is not familiar with. This could require costly product development to make adaptations **[An]**

Import restrictions like tariffs or quotas would increase costs or limit how much soap powder SSM could sell abroad. This would make it harder for SSM to compete on price with local manufacturers, especially with inflation rising **[Ap]** or sell in high enough volumes to achieve economies of scale **[An]**

SSM has no experience selling outside country Y **[Ap]**, so they lack understanding of consumer preferences, competitors, and distribution channels in foreign markets. There are many existing manufacturers in potential new countries **[Ap]**. Without knowledge of these rivals' products, prices and market positioning, SSM would struggle to develop effective marketing strategies. They may also face challenges establishing relationships with new retailers or distributors **[An]**

Of the three problems listed, lack of knowledge is likely to have the greatest effect on SSM's expansion plans **[E]**. While SSM could conduct market research to gain knowledge **[Ap]**, this is expensive and time-consuming. Cultural differences and import restrictions are more easily addressed once SSM understands the new soap powder **[Ap]**market **[E]**. Therefore, lack of knowledge is likely to have the most significant impact on SSM's international expansion plans **[E]**

> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Adapting soap formulas to local tastes → higher acceptance if done correctly
>     - Tailored packaging and marketing → stronger brand relevance in each market
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Product development costs rise for each market variation → squeezes margins
>     - Customized packaging and ads add further expense → total launch costs climb

> 
>   - **Disadvantages**

TT is a large manufacturer of toys based in country Y. It is a public limited company and has been trading for 20 years. TT’s products are designed for children up to the age of 5.

parts.solution_md:
One major benefit is job creation. With unemployment rising in country Z **[Ap]**, TT's new factory would provide much-needed employment for local workers. This could help reduce unemployment and increase incomes, supporting economic growth **[An]**. As TT has well-motivated employees with low turnover **[Ap]**, it is likely they may offer good working conditions and stable jobs **[An]**

Additionally, TT could bring new technology and skills to country Z.  TT uses lean production methods like Kaizen and just-in-time inventory control **[Ap]**, and provides training when introducing new equipment **[Ap]**. This could help improve productivity in the local economy if these practices spread to other businesses **[An]**

However, TT's economies of scale could allow it to undercut local competitors in country Z **[Ap] **on price, potentially leading to job losses in those companies **[An]**

There are also environmental concerns to consider. Building and operating a new factory could increase pollution and resource use in country Z **[Ap].** A government approving a business that has a negative environmental impact could face criticism **[An]**

The government should allow TT to build the factory. The economic benefits of job creation and skills transfer outweigh the drawbacks **[E]**, especially given rising unemployment **[Ap]**. Rejecting TT's investment could mean TT invests in a different country instead **[E]**. However, the government should implement regulations to protect local businesses and the environment, helping country Z gain the most benefit from TT's investment while minimising negative impacts **[E]**

parts.problem_md: Do you think the benefits to a country of having a multinational company located there are always greater than the drawbacks? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Hosting multinational companies can create skilled job opportunities **[K]** which reduces local unemployment and increases the living standards of a country's citizens **[An]**

However, MNCs may try to avoid government taxes** [K]** by locating in areas with tax loopholes, so there is less government income to provide public services **[An]**

Most countries do benefit from multinationals operating in their economy, even if the full amount of tax is not paid **[E]**. The technology transfer and management knowledge that is passed on to local workers can be used to develop other industries and  improve living standards in the long run** [E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Benefits:
>   
>     - Increase number/availability of jobs [k] reduces unemployment [an]
>     - Increase taxes [k] which can be used to improve public services [an]
>     - Increase reputation of country [k] could encourage other businesses to set up/invest in the country [an]
>     - Increasing orders for local suppliers [k] increasing income for local businesses/GDP [an]
>     - Wider choice/quality of goods [k]
>     - Improve infrastructure/new investment/new technology [k]
>     - Knowledge-sharing/new ideas [k]
>   - Drawbacks:
>   
>     - Increased competition [k] reducing sales for local businesses [an] which can force them out of business/reducing revenue [an]
>     - Use up scarce resources [k] so less resources for other uses [an]
>     - Repatriation of profits/send profits back to home country [k] so country does not receive expected amount of tax revenue [an]
>     - Often only unskilled jobs created / may offer low wages/ poor working conditions / exploitation of labour [k]
>     - Often try to avoid/reduce amount of tax paid (in host country) [k]
>     - Power to influence government decisions/local economy [k]
>   - Other appropriate responses should be credited
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Multinational companies create employment opportunities [k] which reduces unemployment [an]. However, they can try to avoid taxes [k] so less funds to provide public services [an]. Countries do benefit from multinationals operating there even if the full amount of tax is not paid, the amount paid can be used to develop the country [eval] which could improve living standards [eval]
